q: Checking that a user is who they claim to be is …
why: Authentication proves identity; authorisation decides what that identity may do.

q: An attacker guesses passwords against your live login page. That is …
why: Online attacks go through your server, so rate limits help. Offline attacks run on a stolen hash database.

q: Validating input in the browser is enough, since the server only receives what the form allows.
why: Myth. Never trust the client: anyone can send any request straight to the server.

q: When an auth check itself errors (say the database is down), the system should …
why: Fail closed: an error must never grant access.
